questions.q: What makes a real test plan different from "it seems to work"?
options: A real test plan is a list of specific, checkable claims -- a given input should produce a given result, and a mismatch is a defect, not a judgment call
A real test plan only needs a final sign-off from one stakeholder
There is no real difference; both approaches confirm a build the same way
A real test plan replaces the need to run the software at all
questions.explain: "Seems to work" is a guess dressed up as confidence. Specific, checkable claims are what make a pass or fail an objective fact, not an opinion.

questions.q: What does TC-03 (a St. Catherine's agent trying to open a Lakeshore record by direct sys_id) confirm when it passes?
options: That the catalog item's variable set is configured correctly
That Domain Separation's own access rules block the cross-domain attempt, not just the queue view's filtering
That St. Catherine's agents have no access to the platform at all
That the integration's API key is valid
questions.explain: TC-03 specifically tests that the block comes from Domain Separation's access rules themselves, which is a stronger guarantee than a queue view simply not showing the record.

questions.q: What is the actual root cause behind TC-06's failure?
options: The PrairieViewHR REST Message returns the wrong employee ID
`upsertWorker` only sets `gr.sys_domain` inside the `if (isNew)` block, so an existing record's domain is never corrected even if it started out wrong
Domain Separation does not support the Prairie View domain at all
The scheduled job that calls the sync is not running on schedule
questions.explain: Reading upsertWorker line by line shows the domain assignment sits only in the new-record branch -- existing records get their name and department refreshed, but never their domain.

questions.q: Why did TC-06 specifically catch this defect when TC-04 and TC-05 did not?
options: TC-06 tested a record that already existed in the wrong domain before the integration went live -- an edge case the clean new-record path never exercises
TC-04 and TC-05 were run incorrectly and should be ignored
TC-06 is unrelated to the upsertWorker function entirely
The defect only affects St. Catherine's and Lakeshore, not Prairie View
questions.explain: TC-04 and TC-05 both exercise paths this script already handled correctly (error handling and new-record coalescing); TC-06 is the one case that exercises the update path's untouched domain field.

questions.q: How is the fix to TC-06 confirmed in this lesson?
options: By writing an entirely new, easier test case after the fix is made
By re-running the exact same TC-06 test case against the corrected script and confirming the director's record and routing now match the expected result
By assuming the fix works because the code change looks correct
By skipping Prairie View's domain entirely and defaulting everyone to the corporate queue
questions.explain: The fix is confirmed with the same test case that found the defect -- moving the domain assignment outside the conditional and rerunning TC-06 to see the corrected result.
